name: stri_split_boundaries
title: Split a String at Text Boundaries

origin.description: Split each string at text boundaries.
origin.usage: stri_split_boundaries(str, n = -1L, tokens_only = FALSE, simplify = FALSE, ..., opts_brkiter = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. A negative value means every piece.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: TRUE keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: FALSE returns a list. TRUE pads a matrix with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: Break-iterator settings. NULL uses the line breaker.

origin.details: Vectorized over str and n. A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip acts as FALSE. Indexes are 1-based inclusive code points. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces and the unsplit remainder unless tokens_only is TRUE. n of 0 is an empty vector. No boundaries yield an empty vector. A missing string or a missing n is one NA. n at least 2147483646 is an error.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, or a character matrix when simplify is not FALSE.
origin.example:
parts <- stri_split_boundaries("hello world foo", type = "word", skip_word_none = TRUE, n = 2)
cat(paste0('stri_split_boundaries("hello world foo", type = "word", skip_word_none = TRUE, n = 2) returns ', paste(parts[[1]], collapse = ", "), '.\n'))

translation.description: Split each string at text boundaries.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. None is an empty vector.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Maximum number of pieces. A negative value means every piece. The value is recycled with str.

arguments.name: tokens_only
arguments.text: True keeps at most n whole pieces and drops the remainder.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: False returns a list. True pads with empty strings. NA pads with NA. The width is at least the largest positive n.

arguments.name: opts_brkiter
arguments.text: A dict of supplied break-iterator settings.

translation.details: A skip_* flag drops every segment whose ending boundary has that ICU rule status. The skipped text is not joined to the next segment. An omitted skip is false. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. BreakIterator indexes are UTF-16 code units and are converted before they are returned. NA stays missing. The string "NA" is text. A positive n returns n - 1 pieces and the unsplit remainder unless tokens_only is true. n of 0 is an empty vector. No boundaries yield an empty vector. A missing string or a missing n is one NA. n at least 2147483646 is an error.
translation.value: A list of character vectors, or a list of rows when simplify is not false.
translation.example:
from stringi.boundary import stri_split_boundaries
parts = stri_split_boundaries("hello world foo", type="word", skip_word_none=True, n=2)
print('stri_split_boundaries("hello world foo", type="word", skip_word_none=True, n=2) returns ' + ", ".join(parts[0]) + ".")
